100.h: 5 - Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī Zayd ibn Sahl ibn al-Aswad * (ع)
100.t:
A companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and of the Banū of his maternal uncles, one of the notables of the Badrīs (البدري), and one of the twelve leaders on the night of al-ʿAqabah.
His name is Zayd ibn Sahl ibn al-Aswad ibn Ḥarām ibn ʿAmr ibn Zayd Manāh ibn ʿAdī ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār al-Khazrajī, al-Najjārī.
He has hadiths.
Narrating from him: ربيبه؛ أنس بن مالك، وزيد بن خالد الجهني، وابن عباس، وابنه؛ أبو إسحاق عبد الله بن أبي طلحة.
He had fasted continuously after the Prophet (1) ﷺ.
He is the one who saw no harm in the fasting person swallowing hail, and would say: It is neither food nor drink (2). ⟦2:27⟧
He is the one about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a troop (1).”
His merits are many.
It is said: He fought on the Roman Sea and died on the ship.
The better known is that he died in Medina and ʿUthmān prayed over him in the year 34 (may Allah be pleased with him).
Ibn Abī ʿArūbah: عن قتادة، عن أنس:
Abū Ṭalḥah, Muʿādh, and Abū ʿUbaydah used to drink ṭilāʾ in Syria, that which was cooked down to a third, two-thirds having gone (2).
I say: It is dibs.
ʿUrwah, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, and Ibn Isḥāq mentioned:
that Abū Ṭalḥah was among those who witnessed al-ʿAqabah and Badr. ⟦2:28⟧
Abū Zurʿah al-Dimashqī said: Abū Ṭalḥah lived forty years after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fasting continuously (1).
I say: Rather, he lived after him some twenty-odd years.
Aḥmad ibn al-Barqī said: Abū Ṭalḥah was a Badrī (البدري), a leader; ʿUthmān prayed over him; about twenty hadiths came from him.
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، وعلي بن زيد، عن أنس:
that his sons said to Abū Ṭalḥah: You have fought in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, so we will fight on your behalf.
He refused, and fought at sea, and died (2).
Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān: عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال:
Abū Ṭalḥah proposed to Umm Sulaym, and she said:
I do desire you, and one like you is not turned away, but you are an unbeliever; if you become Muslim, that is my dowry, and I ask nothing else of you.
So he became Muslim and married her.
Thābit said: We never heard of a dowry more noble than the dowry of Umm Sulaym: Islam (3).
al-Ṭayālisī: حدثنا سليمان بن المغيرة، وحماد، وجعفر بن سليمان، عن ثابت، عن أنس، قال أبو داود:
وحدثناه شيخ سمعه من النضر بن ⟦2:29⟧ أنس:
Mālik - the father of Anas - said to his wife: I see that this man forbids wine.
He went off until he reached Syria, and perished there.
Then Abū Ṭalḥah came proposing to Umm Sulaym, and she said: One like you is not turned away, but you are an unbelieving man, and I want no dowry but Islam.
He said: Who will arrange that for me?
She said: The Prophet ﷺ.
He went off seeking him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Abū Ṭalḥah has come to you with the radiance of Islam between his eyes.”
He said: So he married her on that basis ..., the hadith at length, and how his son by her died, and she concealed it from him and adorned herself for him until he had relations with her, then she informed him, and said:
Allah had lent you a loan, and He took it back, so seek reward for your son (1).
Anas said:
Abū Ṭalḥah said: The sword fell from me on the day of Badr, because of the drowsiness that overcame us (2).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، عن أنس:
that Abū Ṭalḥah fasted for forty years after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, breaking his fast only on the day of Fiṭr or Aḍḥā.
Gharīb (الغريب), meeting the condition of Muslim (3). ⟦2:30⟧
And by it: that Abū Ṭalḥah said: I will not take command over two, nor will I blame them (1).
Thābit narrated from Anas:
that Abū Ṭalḥah used to shoot in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud, and he was a skilled archer.
When Abū Ṭalḥah shot, the Messenger of Allah would raise his sight to see where his arrow fell.
And he would push the chest of the Messenger of Allah with his hand, and say:
O Messenger of Allah, like this, so that no arrow strikes you (2).
ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb narrated from Anas, who said:
On the day of Uḥud, some people fled from the Messenger of Allah, while Abū Ṭalḥah was in front of him, shielding him with a small shield.
He was a skilled archer with a strong draw, and he broke two or three bows that day.
A man would pass by with a quiver of arrows, and he ﷺ would say: “Scatter them for Abū Ṭalḥah.”
Then he would peer toward the enemy, and Abū Ṭalḥah would say: O Prophet of Allah, may my father be your ransom, do not peer out, lest an arrow strike you, my neck before your neck.
He said: I saw ʿĀʾishah and Umm Sulaym, with their garments tucked up (3), I could see the anklets on their legs, as the two of them hurried, with the water-skins on their backs, pouring them into the mouths of the men, then returning and filling them again.
The sword fell from the hand of Abū Ṭalḥah two or three times from drowsiness (4). ⟦2:31⟧
Ibn ʿUyaynah: حدثنا علي بن زيد، عن أنس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a troop (1).”
And when he remained with the Prophet ﷺ, he would kneel in front of him and say:
My soul be a ransom for your soul, and my face a shield for your face (2).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated from Thābit, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah is harder on the polytheists than a troop.”
al-Thawrī: عن عبد الله بن محمد بن عقيل، عن جابر - أو أنس - قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The voice of Abū Ṭalḥah in the army is better than a thousand men” (3).
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة، عن أنس:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Ḥunayn: “Whoever kills an enemy has his spoils.”
Abū Ṭalḥah killed twenty men that day and took their spoils (4).
هشام: عن ابن سيرين، عن أنس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sacrificed and had his head shaved, and he handed the barber his right side, and he shaved it, then he called Abū Ṭalḥah and gave it to him, then ⟦2:32⟧ he handed him his left side, and said: “Shave,” and gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah, who distributed it among the people (1).
Ibn ʿAwn narrated it from Muḥammad (2), and made it mursal (مرسل).
Anas said: Abū Ṭalḥah was the wealthiest of the Anṣār in Medina in palm groves, and he said:
O Messenger of Allah, the dearest of my properties to me is Bayruḥāʾ, and it is a charity for Allah; I hope for its righteousness and its store, so place it, O Messenger of Allah, where Allah shows you.
He said: “Excellent! That is profitable property, and I think you should put it among the relatives (3).”
Ḥumayd narrated from Anas, who said:
After the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Ṭalḥah did not break his fast except on a journey or in illness (4).
Qatādah and Ḥumayd narrated from Anas:
Abū Ṭalḥah used to eat hail while fasting, and say: It is neither food nor drink, it is only a blessing.
ʿAlī ibn Judʿān alone narrated it in this form ⟦2:33⟧ from Anas: and I informed the Messenger of Allah, and he said: “Take from your uncle (1).”
Ḥammād ibn Salamah: عن ثابت، وعلي بن زيد، عن أنس:
that Abū Ṭalḥah recited: “March forth, light and heavy” [Qurʾān 9:42], and said:
Allah has called us to march and has commanded us, our elders and our youths, so equip me.
His sons said: May Allah have mercy on you! You fought in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and we will fight on your behalf now.
He said: So he fought at sea and died, and they found no island to bury him in except after seven days, and he had not changed (2).
He died in the year 34.
Khalīfah alone said: in the year 32.
The hadith master (الحافظ) Abū Muḥammad told us: The Prophet ﷺ shaved one side of his head and distributed it among the people, then shaved his other side and gave it to Abū Ṭalḥah (3).
He said: He was tough, loud-voiced, dark-complexioned, of medium height, and his grey hair did not change colour.
ʿUthmān prayed over him.
It is said: He died in the year 51.
He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ twenty-odd hadiths, of which two are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين).
al-Bukhārī alone has one hadith, and Muslim one (4). ⟦2:34⟧

101.h: 6 - Abū Burdah ibn Niyār ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd al-Balawī * (ع)
101.t:
ibn ʿAmr ibn Kilāb ibn Dahmān al-Balawī, al-Quḍāʿī, al-Anṣārī, of the confederates of the Aws.
His name is Hāniʾ.
He is the maternal uncle of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (1).
He witnessed al-ʿAqabah, Badr, and the Prophet's battles.
He lived on into the reign of Muʿāwiyah.
His hadith is in the Six Books (الكتب الستة).
Narrating from him: ابن أخته البراء، وجابر بن عبد الله، وبشير بن يسار، وغيرهم. ⟦2:35⟧
He was one of the described archers.
It is said: He died in the year 42.

102.h: 7 - Jabr ibn ʿAtīk ibn Qays ibn Hayshah ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī *
102.t:
ibn Umayyah ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn Mālik ibn ʿAwf ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf al-Anṣārī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
A leading Badrī (البدري).
It is said: His name is Jābir.
He had children: ʿAtīk, ʿAbd Allāh, and Umm Thābit.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired him in brotherhood with Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt.
He witnessed Badr and the other battles, and the banner of the Banū Muʿāwiyah ibn Mālik was entrusted to him on the day of the Conquest (1).
al-Wāqidī, Ibn Saʿd, Khalīfah, Ibn Zabr (2), and Ibn Mandah said: He died in the year 61.
It is said: He lived 91 years.
And in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ: عن عبد الله بن عبد الله بن جابر بن عتيك، عن جده لأمه عتيك بن الحارث، قال:
Jābir ibn ʿAtīk informed me:
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to visit ⟦2:36⟧ ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit, and found that he had been overcome, so he said "to Allah we belong and to Him we return", and said: We have been overcome concerning you (1).
I say: The correct view is that Jābir ibn ʿAtīk is the subject of this report and of the report of the date of death, and that Jabr died early, and that Jābir was of the Banū Ghanm ibn Salamah, and Allah knows best.
Their paternal uncle was al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Hayshah al-Awsī (2).
A distinguished Badrī (البدري), counted by: al-Wāqidī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah.
Ibn ʿUqbah did not mention him, nor did Ibn Isḥāq or Abū Maʿshar; rather Ibn Isḥāq and Abū Maʿshar said: Jabr ibn ʿAtīk ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Qays ibn Hayshah.
